reason: While the passage begins with limited collaboration—Moses sending tribal leaders to spy out the land—the overwhelming narrative arc depicts conflict and breakdown between leaders and people. The text primarily shows the congregation's rebellion against Moses and Aaron, with the people threatening to stone Joshua and Caleb, murmuring against their leaders ('וַיִּלֹּנוּ עַל־ מֹשֶׁה וְעַל־ אַהֲרֹן'), and expressing deep distrust. The spies' negative report divides rather than unites the people and leadership. God's subsequent judgment on the congregation for refusing to follow leadership further underscores the antagonistic rather than collaborative relationship. The text emphasizes discord, rebellion, and the failure of the people to work with their leaders toward the promised goal.
